_comment: Teaching/lore NPC on the actor model (plan-entity-model.md chunk 3a) — formerly a statless model/npc type placed from zone.npcs, now an ordinary actor carrying an interaction block. role creature + speed 0 (PO 2026-07-27, D4): an NPC is an actor that authors no movement, not a kind of its own. Unattackable by two AUTHORED knobs (D5): faction townsfolk (friendlyToPlayers ⇒ player damage skips it) and collisionLayer 97 = PlayerStatic(1) + Viewport(32) + MobStatic(64) — solid and streamed, but deliberately NOT on Action(2), so no aura on either side can target it. interaction.range 2.0 [PLACEHOLDER] is the talk reach and sizes the one sensor. experience 0 keeps it off the nameplate path; the health bar is accepted (D3). All values [PLACEHOLDER]. The village hermit: first aid for yourself, then healing for others — and, from level 10, the two beast-handling cooldowns (Calm, CharmBeast) plan-faction-flips.md shipped without a source. ⚑ QUESTS: offers and turns in `village-welcome`, the tutorial-shaped talk_to errand. ⚑ Q4 SHAPE (conversation-journal §4.6, R1): greeting at root, teachings behind one row as four NAMED one-grant rows (the old nameless multi-grant walls opened the panel on a wall of greyed skill rows), the quest behind its own row with its brief as that node's text plus a follow-up answer-node. Quest rows carry NO quest_at_stage gate — a row is shown iff its ledger op would succeed (the Q1 show-rule), so Accept vanishes once taken, the turn-in appears exactly when walkable, and the question stays askable throughout.
name: Hermit

lines: Did you break your nose recently? Doesn't look good.
A stranger dies quicker than a face people know.
Two faces worth the walk: the farmer at his field, the crier in the square. Be seen by both, then come back.

grants.line: The farmer and the crier. Neither of them bites, whatever the crier would have you believe.
Good. That's the whole of it — the village knows your face now.

lines: A known face gets pulled out of the ditch. A stranger gets stepped over.
Out here that is the whole of the law.
Sit still, then. What is it you need?

grants.line: Let me show you how to tend to those wounds...
Let me show you how to tend to the wounds of your allies...
Most things that snarl at you would rather not. Let me show you how to ask them to stop.
And if you ask well enough, some of them will walk beside you for a while.
